subject: Private deployment: request for BYOK evidence pack and operator-access assurances
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicore.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medicore.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Private deploy evidence request (BYOK and operator access)

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we move toward a private deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway) for our EU clinical workloads, Legal and Security have a few concrete asks before procurement will proceed:

1) A signed BYOK attestation that outlines Redwood's responsibilities vs customer responsibilities (key rotation, escrow triggers, operator access scenarios).
2) A current subprocessor list with geographic footprints and confirmation that no subprocessor will have unescorted access to decrypted data for this deployment.
3) A brief runbook describing breakglass/operator access: who can request it, what logs are captured, and how Medicore will be notified.
4) Any export controls or cross-border transfer documentation relevant to EU data residency.

Can you share an "evidence pack" with the above items and an ETA for delivery? Procurement would also like to see the narrow contract language we can put into the DPA to limit operator access and require two-person authorization for emergency key unwrapping.

Best,
Elena

Elena Morales
Head of Security Operations
Medicore Health

Attachments: none

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicore.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deploy evidence request (BYOK and operator access)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We'll compile an evidence pack. High-level plan below and proposed ETA: EOD Thursday (2026-12-03) for an initial bundle; signed BYOK attestation available via DocuSign by next Monday if that works.

Summary of what we'll include now:
- BYOK attestation (scope: customer-owned CMKs, responsibilities matrix).
- Current subprocessor inventory (CSV + PDF) with facility country and role (compute/monitoring/backup).
- Operator access runbook (procedural summary + sample audit log).
- Cross-border/transfer note referencing our standard data routing policies and exception process.

Operational notes:
- For private deployments we support tenant-controlled key material (BYOK) with optional local HSM integration. Redwood operators do not have access to plaintext unless a documented breakglass process is triggered.
- Breakglass requires approval from two named Redwood approvers + customer delegated approver; full session capture and immutable logs are retained for 7 years by default (we can align retention with Medicore's retention).

Irene (cc) will prepare the subprocessor list and runbook snippets; Ben will coordinate the attestation language with Legal.

Next steps:
- Irene: assemble subprocessor list + runbook excerpts (ETA 2026-12-02 18:00 UTC).
- Ben: draft BYOK attestation for DocuSign (ETA 2026-12-03).
- I'll share a short DPA addendum text we recommend for the operator access & two-person auth clause.

Avery
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_list_20261201.pdf (will follow), operator_access_runbook_v1.2.pdf (draft)

From: Marco Silvestri <msilvestri@lawfirm-eu.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@medicore.com, elena.morales@medicore.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 06:20:00 +0000
Subject: Contract language suggestion for two-person operator unwrapping

Avery/Ben —

Per Medicore's counsel review, we propose inserting an addendum to the DPA with the following essentials:
- Definition of "Breakglass": the narrow, time-limited procedure permitting temporary operator-assisted key unwrapping only when the customer explicitly documents an emergency and requests assistance.
- Two-person rule: two independent Redwood approvers AND one Medicore approver must authorize.
- Mandatory capture: session recording, tamper-evident logs, and immediate notification to the Medicore security contact.
- Evidence: Redwood must deliver a signed incident report within 48 hours and provide raw logs within 7 business days under a secure transfer mechanism.

Please flag if Redwood cannot meet any of the above; this will be part of the procurement gating criteria.

Regards,
Marco
Partner, Data & Privacy Practice

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco Silvestri <msilvestri@lawfirm-eu.com>, elena.morales@medicore.com
Cc: avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Contract language suggestion for two-person operator unwrapping

Marco / Elena — thanks for the precise language. We can support all bulleted items with these clarifications: 

1) Subprocessors: enclosed PDF lists subprocessors and whether they process metadata only or have opportunity for content-level access. For this Medicore VPC/on-prem config, the listed monitoring/infra subprocessors are contractually restricted from accessing decrypted content; that restriction is enforced by our runtime and contractual SSO bindings.

2) Two-person rule: Redwood confirms two independent internal approvers plus the Medicore approver is an acceptable model. We recommend naming roles (e.g., Infrastructure Lead, Security Oncall) in the DPA with a process for temporary role substitution.

3) Logs & evidence: runbook (attached) shows the breakglass flow and sample log extract. We retain an immutable audit trail; we can deliver encrypted logs to a pre-agreed SFTP or Azure Blob container.

4) Escrow / key release: BYOK attestation clarifies we do not hold plaintext keys; escrow is available only under mutually agreed legal triggers and a notarized process. We will prepare a short clause and a DocuSign-ready attestation for Medicore's signature.

I attached: redwood_subprocessor_list_20261201.pdf ; operator_access_runbook_v1.2.pdf ; preliminary byok_attestation_signed.pdf (unsigned template with signatory block).

If Procurement wants specific retention windows or analytics redaction, let us know and we will adjust the addendum language.

Thanks,
Irene
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_list_20261201.pdf, operator_access_runbook_v1.2.pdf, byok_attestation_signed.pdf

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicore.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

Perfect — this addresses our asks. Procurement will review the attached PDFs and loop Legal for the DPA addendum.

Quick Q: what is the expected timeline for the signed BYOK attestation (DocuSign)? If Ben can get that ready by Monday as Avery suggested, we can keep the procurement window to three business days. Also please confirm the final location/process for receiving encrypted logs (we prefer an Azure container with a pre-shared access token).

I'll mark this as high priority on our side.

Best,
Elena
